- Scenario: SQL is "insert into target select user_id, user_name from source". The physical target table columns are id, name.

- There is no logic to derive target columns from the target table schema via MetaDataProvider when target columns are not specified in the SQL. Therefore, the code incorrectly uses SELECT list column names on the target side.

    33→class SourceHandler(SourceHandlerMixin, NextTokenBaseHandler):
    34→    """Source Table & Column Handler."""
    35→
    36→    SOURCE_TABLE_TOKENS = (
    37→        r"FROM",
    38→        # inspired by https://github.com/andialbrecht/sqlparse/blob/master/sqlparse/keywords.py
    39→        r"((LEFT\s+|RIGHT\s+|FULL\s+)?(INNER\s+|OUTER\s+|STRAIGHT\s+)?|(CROSS\s+|NATURAL\s+)?)?JOIN",
    40→    )
    41→
    42→    def __init__(self):
    43→        self.column_flag = False
    44→        self.columns = []
    45→        self.tables = []
    46→        self.union_barriers = []
    47→        super().__init__()
    48→
    49→    def _indicate(self, token: Token) -> bool:
    50→        if token.normalized in ("UNION", "UNION ALL"):
    51→            self.union_barriers.append((len(self.columns), len(self.tables)))
    52→
    53→        if self.column_flag is True and bool(token.normalized == "DISTINCT"):
    54→            # special handling for SELECT DISTINCT
    55→            return True
    56→
    57→        if any(re.match(regex, token.normalized) for regex in self.SOURCE_TABLE_TOKENS):
    58→            self.column_flag = False
    59→            return True
    60→        elif bool(token.normalized == "SELECT"):
    61→            self.column_flag = True
    62→            return True
    63→        else:
    64→            return False
    65→

    67→        if self.column_flag:
    68→            self._handle_column(token)
    69→        else:
    70→            self._handle_table(token, holder)

    72→    def _handle_table(self, token: Token, holder: SubQueryLineageHolder) -> None:

    74→            self._add_dataset_from_identifier(token, holder)
    75→        elif isinstance(token, IdentifierList):
    76→            # This is to support join in ANSI-89 syntax
    77→            for identifier in token.get_sublists():
    78→                self._add_dataset_from_identifier(identifier, holder)
    79→        elif isinstance(token, Parenthesis):

    81→                # SELECT col1 FROM (SELECT col2 FROM tab1), the subquery will be parsed as Parenthesis
    82→                # This syntax without alias for subquery is invalid in MySQL, while valid for SparkSQL
    83→                self.tables.append(SqlParseSubQuery.of(token, None))

    94→                        isinstance(t, Parenthesis) and using_flag is False

    99→        elif isinstance(token, Function):
   100→            # functions like unnest or generator can output a sequence of values as source, ignore it for now
   101→            pass
   102→        else:
   103→            raise SQLLineageException(
   104→                "An Identifier is expected, got %s[value: %s] instead."
   105→                % (type(token).__name__, token)
   106→            )

   108→    def _handle_column(self, token: Token) -> None:
   109→        column_token_types = (Identifier, Function, Operation, Case, Parenthesis)
   110→        if isinstance(token, column_token_types) or token.ttype is Wildcard:
   111→            column_tokens = [token]
   112→        elif isinstance(token, IdentifierList):
   113→            column_tokens = [
   114→                sub_token
   115→                for sub_token in token.tokens

   117→                    isinstance(sub_token, column_token_types)
   118→                    and not sub_token.value.startswith(
   119→                        "@"
   120→                    )  # ignore tsql variable column starts with @
   121→                )
   122→                or sub_token.ttype is Wildcard  # For case like: select a.col, b.*
   123→            ]

   125→            # SELECT constant value will end up here
   126→            column_tokens = []
   127→        for token in column_tokens:
   128→            self.columns.append(SqlParseColumn.of(token))

   130→    def _add_dataset_from_identifier(
   131→        self, identifier: Identifier, holder: SubQueryLineageHolder

   133→        first_token = identifier.token_first(skip_cm=True)
   134→        if isinstance(first_token, Function):
   135→            # function() as alias, no dataset involved
   136→            return None
   137→        elif isinstance(first_token, Parenthesis) and is_values_clause(first_token):
   138→            # (VALUES ...) AS alias, no dataset involved
   139→            return None

   143→            dataset = Path(path_match.groups()[1])

   146→            subqueries = get_subquery_parentheses(identifier)
   147→            if len(subqueries) > 0:
   148→                # SELECT col1 FROM (SELECT col2 FROM tab1) dt, the subquery will be parsed as Identifier
   149→                # referring https://github.com/andialbrecht/sqlparse/issues/218 for further information
   150→                parenthesis, alias = subqueries[0]
   151→                read = SqlParseSubQuery.of(parenthesis, alias)
   152→            else:

   155→                    cte = cte_dict.get(
   156→                        escape_identifier_name(identifier.get_real_name())
   157→                    )

   160→                        read = SqlParseSubQuery.of(
   161→                            cte.query,
   162→                            identifier.get_alias() or identifier.get_real_name(),
   163→                        )
   164→                if read is None:
   165→                    read = SqlParseTable.of(identifier)
   166→            dataset = read
   167→        if dataset:
   168→            self.tables.append(dataset)

   247→class StatementLineageHolder(SubQueryLineageHolder, ColumnLineageMixin):
   248→    """
   249→    Statement Level Lineage Result.
   250→
   251→    Based on SubQueryLineageHolder, StatementLineageHolder holds extra attributes like drop and rename
   252→
   253→    For drop, it is a Set[:class:`sqllineage.core.models.Table`].
   254→
   255→    For rename, it a Set[Tuple[:class:`sqllineage.core.models.Table`, :class:`sqllineage.core.models.Table`]],
   256→    with the first table being original table before renaming and the latter after renaming.
   257→    """
   258→
   259→    def __str__(self):
   260→        return "\n".join(
   261→            f"table {attr}: {sorted(getattr(self, attr), key=lambda x: str(x)) if getattr(self, attr) else '[]'}"
   262→            for attr in ["read", "write", "cte", "drop", "rename"]
   263→        )
   264→
   265→    def __repr__(self):
   266→        return str(self)
   267→
   268→    @property
   269→    def read(self) -> Set[Table]:  # type: ignore
   270→        return {t for t in super().read if isinstance(t, DATASET_CLASSES)}
   271→
   272→    @property
   273→    def write(self) -> Set[Table]:  # type: ignore
   274→        return {t for t in super().write if isinstance(t, DATASET_CLASSES)}
   275→
   276→    @property
   277→    def drop(self) -> Set[Table]:
   278→        return self._property_getter(NodeTag.DROP)  # type: ignore
   279→
   280→    def add_drop(self, value) -> None:
   281→        self._property_setter(value, NodeTag.DROP)
   282→
   283→    @property
   284→    def rename(self) -> Set[Tuple[Table, Table]]:
   285→        return {
   286→            (src, tgt)
   287→            for src, tgt, attr in self.graph.edges(data=True)
   288→            if attr.get("type") == EdgeType.RENAME
   289→        }
   290→
   291→    def add_rename(self, src: Table, tgt: Table) -> None:
   292→        self.graph.add_edge(src, tgt, type=EdgeType.RENAME)
   293→
   294→    @staticmethod
   295→    def of(holder: SubQueryLineageHolder) -> "StatementLineageHolder":
   296→        stmt_holder = StatementLineageHolder()
   297→        stmt_holder.graph = holder.graph

   301→class SQLLineageHolder(ColumnLineageMixin):
   302→    def __init__(self, graph: DiGraph):
   303→        """
   304→        The combined lineage result in representation of Directed Acyclic Graph.
   305→
   306→        :param graph: the Directed Acyclic Graph holding all the combined lineage result.
   307→        """
   308→        self.graph = graph
   309→        self._selfloop_tables = self.__retrieve_tag_tables(NodeTag.SELFLOOP)
   310→        self._sourceonly_tables = self.__retrieve_tag_tables(NodeTag.SOURCE_ONLY)
   311→        self._targetonly_tables = self.__retrieve_tag_tables(NodeTag.TARGET_ONLY)
   312→
   313→    @property
   314→    def table_lineage_graph(self) -> DiGraph:
   315→        """
   316→        The table level DiGraph held by SQLLineageHolder
   317→        """
   318→        table_nodes = [n for n in self.graph.nodes if isinstance(n, DATASET_CLASSES)]
   319→        return self.graph.subgraph(table_nodes)
   320→
   321→    @property
   322→    def column_lineage_graph(self) -> DiGraph:
   323→        """
   324→        The column level DiGraph held by SQLLineageHolder
   325→        """
   326→        column_nodes = [n for n in self.graph.nodes if isinstance(n, Column)]
   327→        return self.graph.subgraph(column_nodes)
   328→
   329→    @property
   330→    def source_tables(self) -> Set[Table]:
   331→        """
   332→        a list of source :class:`sqllineage.core.models.Table`
   333→        """
   334→        source_tables = {
   335→            table for table, deg in self.table_lineage_graph.in_degree if deg == 0
   336→        }.intersection(
   337→            {table for table, deg in self.table_lineage_graph.out_degree if deg > 0}
   338→        )
   339→        source_tables |= self._selfloop_tables
   340→        source_tables |= self._sourceonly_tables
   341→        return source_tables
   342→
   343→    @property
   344→    def target_tables(self) -> Set[Table]:
   345→        """
   346→        a list of target :class:`sqllineage.core.models.Table`
   347→        """
   348→        target_tables = {
   349→            table for table, deg in self.table_lineage_graph.out_degree if deg == 0
   350→        }.intersection(
   351→            {table for table, deg in self.table_lineage_graph.in_degree if deg > 0}
   352→        )
   353→        target_tables |= self._selfloop_tables
   354→        target_tables |= self._targetonly_tables
   355→        return target_tables
   356→
   357→    @property
   358→    def intermediate_tables(self) -> Set[Table]:
   359→        """
   360→        a list of intermediate :class:`sqllineage.core.models.Table`
   361→        """
   362→        intermediate_tables = {
   363→            table for table, deg in self.table_lineage_graph.in_degree if deg > 0
   364→        }.intersection(
   365→            {table for table, deg in self.table_lineage_graph.out_degree if deg > 0}
   366→        )
   367→        intermediate_tables -= self.__retrieve_tag_tables(NodeTag.SELFLOOP)
   368→        return intermediate_tables
   369→
   370→    def __retrieve_tag_tables(self, tag) -> Set[Union[Path, Table]]:
   371→        return {
   372→            table
   373→            for table, attr in self.graph.nodes(data=True)
   374→            if attr.get(tag) is True and isinstance(table, DATASET_CLASSES)
   375→        }
   376→
   377→    @staticmethod
   378→    def _build_digraph(
   379→        metadata_provider: MetaDataProvider, *args: StatementLineageHolder
   380→    ) -> DiGraph:
   381→        g = DiGraph()
   382→        for holder in args:
   383→            g = nx.compose(g, holder.graph)
   384→            if holder.drop:
   385→                for table in holder.drop:
   386→                    if g.has_node(table) and g.degree[table] == 0:
   387→                        g.remove_node(table)
   388→            elif holder.rename:
   389→                for table_old, table_new in holder.rename:
   390→                    g = nx.relabel_nodes(g, {table_old: table_new})
   391→                    g.remove_edge(table_new, table_new)
   392→                    if g.degree[table_new] == 0:
   393→                        g.remove_node(table_new)
   394→            else:
   395→                read, write = holder.read, holder.write
   396→                if len(read) > 0 and len(write) == 0:
   397→                    # source only table comes from SELECT statement
   398→                    nx.set_node_attributes(
   399→                        g, {table: True for table in read}, NodeTag.SOURCE_ONLY
   400→                    )
   401→                elif len(read) == 0 and len(write) > 0:
   402→                    # target only table comes from case like: 1) INSERT/UPDATE constant values; 2) CREATE TABLE
   403→                    nx.set_node_attributes(
   404→                        g, {table: True for table in write}, NodeTag.TARGET_ONLY
   405→                    )
   406→                else:
   407→                    for source, target in itertools.product(read, write):
   408→                        g.add_edge(source, target, type=EdgeType.LINEAGE)
   409→        nx.set_node_attributes(
   410→            g,
   411→            {table: True for table in {e[0] for e in nx.selfloop_edges(g)}},
   412→            NodeTag.SELFLOOP,
   413→        )
   414→        # find all the columns that we can't assign accurately to a parent table (with multiple parent candidates)
   415→        unresolved_cols = [
   416→            (s, t)
   417→            for s, t in g.edges
   418→            if isinstance(s, Column) and len(s.parent_candidates) > 1
   419→        ]
   420→        for unresolved_col, tgt_col in unresolved_cols:
   421→            # check if there's only one parent candidate contains the column with same name
   422→            src_cols = []
   423→            # check if source column exists in graph (either from subquery or from table created in prev statement)
   424→            for parent in unresolved_col.parent_candidates:
   425→                src_col = Column(unresolved_col.raw_name)
   426→                src_col.parent = parent
   427→                if g.has_edge(parent, src_col):
   428→                    src_cols.append(src_col)
   429→            # if not in graph, check if defined in table schema by metadata service
   430→            if len(src_cols) == 0 and bool(metadata_provider):
   431→                for parent in unresolved_col.parent_candidates:
   432→                    if (
   433→                        isinstance(parent, Table)
   434→                        and str(parent.schema) != Schema.unknown
   435→                    ):
   436→                        columns = metadata_provider.get_table_columns(parent)
   437→                        for src_col in columns:
   438→                            if unresolved_col.raw_name == src_col.raw_name:
   439→                                src_cols.append(src_col)
   440→
   441→            # Multiple sources is a correct case for JOIN with USING
   442→            # It incorrect for JOIN with ON, but sql without specifying an alias in this case will be invalid
   443→            for src_col in src_cols:
   444→                g.add_edge(src_col, tgt_col, type=EdgeType.LINEAGE)
   445→            if len(src_cols) > 0:
   446→                # only delete unresolved column when it's resolved
   447→                g.remove_edge(unresolved_col, tgt_col)
   448→
   449→        # when unresolved column got resolved, it will be orphan node, and we can remove it
   450→        for node in [n for n, deg in g.degree if deg == 0]:
   451→            if isinstance(node, Column) and len(node.parent_candidates) > 1:
   452→                g.remove_node(node)
   453→        return g
   454→
   455→    @staticmethod
   456→    def of(metadata_provider, *args: StatementLineageHolder) -> "SQLLineageHolder":
   457→        """
   458→        To assemble multiple :class:`sqllineage.core.holders.StatementLineageHolder` into
   459→        :class:`sqllineage.core.holders.SQLLineageHolder`
   460→        """
   461→        g = SQLLineageHolder._build_digraph(metadata_provider, *args)
   462→        return SQLLineageHolder(g)

    43→    def analyze(
    44→        self, sql: str, metadata_provider: MetaDataProvider
    45→    ) -> StatementLineageHolder:
    46→        # get rid of comments, which cause inconsistencies in sqlparse output
    47→        stmt = sqlparse.parse(trim_comment(sql))[0]
    48→        if (
    49→            stmt.get_type() == "DELETE"
    50→            or stmt.token_first(skip_cm=True).normalized == "TRUNCATE"
    51→            or stmt.token_first(skip_cm=True).normalized.upper() == "REFRESH"
    52→            or stmt.token_first(skip_cm=True).normalized == "CACHE"
    53→            or stmt.token_first(skip_cm=True).normalized.upper() == "UNCACHE"
    54→            or stmt.token_first(skip_cm=True).normalized == "SHOW"
    55→        ):
    56→            holder = StatementLineageHolder()
    57→        elif stmt.get_type() == "DROP":
    58→            holder = self._extract_from_ddl_drop(stmt)
    59→        elif (
    60→            stmt.get_type() == "ALTER"
    61→            or stmt.token_first(skip_cm=True).normalized == "RENAME"
    62→        ):
    63→            holder = self._extract_from_ddl_alter(stmt)
    64→        elif stmt.get_type() == "MERGE":
    65→            holder = self._extract_from_dml_merge(stmt, metadata_provider)
    66→        else:
    67→            # DML parsing logic also applies to CREATE DDL
    68→            holder = StatementLineageHolder.of(
    69→                self._extract_from_dml(stmt, AnalyzerContext(), metadata_provider)
    70→            )

    74→    def _extract_from_ddl_drop(cls, stmt: Statement) -> StatementLineageHolder:
    75→        holder = StatementLineageHolder()
    76→        for table in {
    77→            SqlParseTable.of(t) for t in stmt.tokens if isinstance(t, Identifier)
    78→        }:
    79→            holder.add_drop(table)
    80→        return holder

    82→    @classmethod
    83→    def _extract_from_ddl_alter(cls, stmt: Statement) -> StatementLineageHolder:
    84→        holder = StatementLineageHolder()
    85→        tables = []
    86→        for t in stmt.tokens:
    87→            if isinstance(t, Identifier):
    88→                tables.append(SqlParseTable.of(t))
    89→            elif isinstance(t, IdentifierList):
    90→                for identifier in t.get_identifiers():
    91→                    tables.append(SqlParseTable.of(identifier))
    92→        keywords = [t for t in stmt.tokens if t.is_keyword]
    93→        if any(k.normalized == "RENAME" for k in keywords):
    94→            if stmt.get_type() == "ALTER" and len(tables) == 2:
    95→                holder.add_rename(tables[0], tables[1])
    96→            elif (
    97→                stmt.token_first(skip_cm=True).normalized == "RENAME"
    98→                and len(tables) % 2 == 0
    99→            ):
   100→                for i in range(0, len(tables), 2):
   101→                    holder.add_rename(tables[i], tables[i + 1])
   102→        if any(k.normalized == "EXCHANGE" for k in keywords) and len(tables) == 2:
   103→            holder.add_write(tables[0])

   110→        stmt: Statement,
   111→        metadata_provider: MetaDataProvider,
   112→    ) -> StatementLineageHolder:
   113→        holder = StatementLineageHolder()
   114→        src_flag = tgt_flag = update_flag = insert_flag = False
   115→        insert_columns = []
   116→        direct_source: Optional[Union[Table, SubQuery]] = None
   117→        for token in stmt.tokens:

   127→                elif token.normalized == "INSERT":
   128→                    insert_flag = True

   130→                    update_flag = False
   131→                continue
   132→
   133→            if tgt_flag:

   145→                                metadata_provider,
